title: 观书有感·其一
author: 朱熹
intro: A clear little pond reflects the sky and clouds. Why is it so clear? Because fresh water keeps flowing in from its source — and a mind stays clear the same way, by always learning.
analysis: 这首诗题目叫“观书有感”（读书有感想），可是诗里一个字也没写书，只写了一个池塘。前两句写半亩大的方形池塘，像一面打开的镜子，天光和云影都映在水里，一起来回晃动。第三句诗人问池塘：你怎么能这样清澈？第四句回答：因为有源头不断地流来新鲜的活水。这就是诗的道理：人要心里明白、思想清楚，就要不断读书、学习新知识，像池塘需要源头活水一样。诗人把一个抽象的道理放在一个具体的画面里，这叫“寓理于景”（把道理藏在景物里），所以读起来不枯燥。“源头活水”今天是常用语，比喻事物发展的动力和来源。
analysisEn: The title is “Thoughts on Reading”, yet the poem never mentions a book — it describes a pond. A square pond, about half a mu across, lies open like a mirror; the light of the sky and the shadows of clouds move back and forth together across it. Then the poet asks the pond a question: “How can you be so clear?” And answers it: “Because living water keeps coming from the source.” That is the point. A mind stays clear and sharp only if it keeps taking in something new — by reading, studying, thinking — just as a pond stays clean only while fresh water flows in. A pond with no inflow goes stagnant. Zhu Xi puts an abstract idea inside a concrete picture, a method Chinese critics call yù lǐ yú jǐng (“hiding a principle in a scene”), so the lesson never feels like a lecture. The phrase 源头活水 (“living water from the source”) is used every day in modern Chinese for whatever keeps something fresh and growing — new ideas, new people, new learning.
background: Zhu Xi (1130–1200) was the most influential Confucian philosopher after Confucius himself; his commentaries became the basis of the imperial exams for some 600 years. This is the first of two poems with this title; the second describes a great ship floating free on spring floods.
pronunciation: 那得：那 读 nǎ（同“哪”，“怎么”），按通行注音读 nǎ，不读 nà。为有：为 读 wèi（因为）。一鉴 jiàn。渠 qú（它，指方塘）。
version: 采用统编语文教材文本。《观书有感》共两首，网站选第一首（“半亩方塘一鉴开”），第二首为“昨夜江边春水生”。

lines.py: bàn mǔ fāng táng yī jiàn kāi
lines.lit: A half-mu square pond opens like a mirror;
lines.en: A small square pond lies open like a mirror;

lines.py: tiān guāng yún yǐng gòng pái huái
lines.lit: sky light and cloud shadows together move back and forth.
lines.en: sky light and cloud shadows drift across it together.

lines.py: wèn qú nǎ dé qīng rú xǔ
lines.lit: I ask it: how can it be so clear?
lines.en: I ask the pond: how do you stay so clear?

lines.py: wèi yǒu yuán tóu huó shuǐ lái
lines.lit: Because there is living water coming from the source.
lines.en: Because fresh water keeps flowing from its source.

words.en: half a mu (a small area, about 330 m²)
words.note: 亩：中国传统面积单位，今天农村仍用。
塘：水池，现代汉语“池塘”“鱼塘”。
古代的镜子。现代汉语“借鉴”“以史为鉴”还保留“镜子”的意思。

words.en: light of the sky and shadows of clouds
words.note: 今天也作写景的常用语。
这里指光影在水中晃动。现代多指人来回走或犹豫。
古义：第三人称“它”。现代汉语“渠”指水渠、渠道。
书面语，现代说“这样”“如此”。
今天常用，比喻事物不断发展的来源和动力。

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 清澈的池水比喻人清明的头脑；源头活水比喻不断学习得来的新知识。
imagery.en: The clear pond is a clear mind; the living water from the source is the new knowledge that keeps it clear.

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 云影映在水里，说明池水清得像镜子。
imagery.en: Clouds reflected in the water show how mirror-clear the pond is.
